name: Stables (The Stables, Phase I)
award: 2024 Federal 4% and state housing tax credits (Round Two)
headline: Grovewood Community Development's The Stables is an 85-unit new-construction family building for households at 30% to 80% AMI on the 4.79-acre former Aurora Horse Boarding Stables site at 10850 E. Exposition Avenue, Aurora; it won 2024 Round Two federal 4% and accelerated state credits from CHFA, with $22.56M of CHFA bonds, and broke ground by early February 2026.
why_it_matters: It shows how a nonprofit stacked city and county money (CDBG, HOME, ARPA, PAB cap transfers) with state AHIF acquisition debt to win an infill site against market-rate bidders, and it is one of the few 2024 Round Two deals with a dated groundbreaking.

status.label: Groundbreaking reported 2026-02-02; completion not yet public
status.detail: Mile High CRE and ColoradoBiz reported on 2026-02-02 that Grovewood had broken ground on Phase I, naming the lender, equity investors and general contractor. No public record of the bond closing date, building permit number or completion date was found; the application had targeted a fourth-quarter 2025 construction start.

next_step: Watch for a lease-up or completion notice and for any CHFA or city record of the Phase II senior building (49 or 52 units).

key_numbers.meaning: 11 one-bedroom, 56 two-bedroom and 18 three-bedroom units, income-averaged at 30% to 80% AMI (average 55.6%).
About $20.4M over 10 years, plus $1,800,000 of accelerated state credit.
Tax-exempt construction bonds through a CHFA risk-share loan, using CHFA cap plus cap transferred from the City of Aurora ($3.7M) and Arapahoe County ($5.0M conditionally committed).
Calcon Constructors is the general contractor and Shopworks Architecture the architect.

facts.value: 10850 East Exposition Avenue, Aurora 80012 (just east of S. Havana Street)
The applicant report shows the same federal credit ($2,040,378), state credit ($1,800,000) and bond amount ($22,560,000) as the award

4.79 acres, former Aurora Horse Boarding Stables (in operation on the site since 1947); census tract 801, a Qualified Census Tract; Rangeview/Expo Park area next to Exposition Park and the Highline Canal Trail
Rezoned from R-1 to R-4 by Aurora City Council on 2024-06-10; site plan, final plat and building permits were still ahead at application
One four-story, 85-unit wood-frame (Type V-A) building with two elevators, gabled roofs and lap siding/brick that echo the former stable; trauma-informed design
Two-phase intergenerational campus: Phase I 85 family units, Phase II senior (62+) units
Enterprise Green Communities; electrification-ready (CHFA: all-electric-ready design)
RTD Route 105 stop at S. Havana and Exposition about 0.3 mile away; Florida light rail station about 3 miles
Phase I found no recognized environmental conditions; Arapahoe County completed the NEPA review
Overall capture rate 11.3%; LIHTC vacancy in the market area at or near 0%; lease-up projected at 20 units a month

money.source: Colorado accelerated state housing tax credit
money.note: Sugar Creek Capital is named among the equity sources; its role as state credit buyer is inferred.

Construction-period bonds via CHFA risk-share loan, public sale; permanent bonds $11,395,000; taxable construction loan $6,194,673 (application figures). Cap from CHFA plus transfers from the City of Aurora and Arapahoe County.

background.text: The stables site stayed with one family from 1947 until Grovewood bought it in August 2023; the application says the sellers chose Grovewood over market-rate bidders because of the affordable housing use. No purchase price was found in public records reviewed.

Aurora City Council approved the rezoning from R-1 agricultural to R-4 high-density residential on 2024-06-10, after a 2024-04-09 community meeting; the applicant reports no local opposition and letters of support from the Ward 3 council member, an Arapahoe County commissioner, Cherry Creek School District and the Village East Neighborhood Association.
Value engineering cut about $1.9M of hard cost; Phase I carries most of the site work for both phases (stormwater, utilities and access off Exposition Avenue).

The project is not set aside for homeless or special-needs households, though Grovewood's mission includes residents with developmental disabilities, mental illness or substance use disorders; no project-based vouchers are described.

Grovewood owns 282 units across nine properties in Aurora, Englewood and Littleton and was finishing the 81-unit Sapling Grove Apartments in Aurora; Exponent, an existing LIHTC property, adjoins the site.

Mile High CRE says the site adjoins Aurora Housing Authority property; the Aurora Housing Authority is named as a funding partner, but the terms (for example a tax-exemption partnership) are not public.

discrepancies.text: The CHFA application and Connect CRE describe a 134-unit campus with a 49-unit senior Phase II, while the groundbreaking coverage describes 137 units with a 52-unit senior Phase II.

Connect CRE lists Proposition 123 funding among the sources, while the CHFA application lists no Proposition 123 money (its state money is a Division of Housing AHIF land loan through Impact Development Fund).
